newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Ceval to invest in soy facilities.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Ceval to invest in soy facilities.

text.p: Brazilian food processor Ceval Alimentos SA will invest $30 million by the end of 1998 in building two warehouses and a soybean crushing facility in the northern Brazilian port of Itaqui, the company said in a statement.
Ceval said it planned to invest $5 million immediately with the remaining money invested over the next two years.

Director-general Vilmar de Oliveira Schurmann said that in the next six months, Ceval would build a warehouse for soybeans with a capacity of 30,000 tonnes and another for soymeal with capacity of 50,000 tonnes.
Both would be ready in time for the next harvest.
The soybean crushing facility, with a capacity of 2,000 tonnes per day, should start operating at the end of 1998, Schurmann added.
Ceval also has an option to build a soyoil refinery and a margarine factory at an unspecified point in the future.
Schurmann emphasized the importance of the location of the new facilities.

"We are close to New Orleans and the Gulf of Mexico, from where we will be able to import soybeans under the draw-back regime, in order to supply the unit in between Brazilian harvests," Shurmann said.

Cerval said it had received fiscal benefits from the state of Maranhao and would build the new facilities on land leased to it by state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce in a renewable 20-year contract.
Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso was scheduled to attend the contract signing ceremony on Saturday.
